content.body:
Designed in 1936, the Dewoitine D.520 was the best French-designed fighter of the War. A successor to the Moraine-Saulnier MS.406, the D.520 was fast, maneuverable, and well-armed with a single 20mm canon firing through the spinner and four 7.5 mm machineguns in the wings.
With the fall of France in 1940, the D.520 went on to serve for the Vichy forces in North Africa, fighting alongside and against both Allied and Axis aircraft. Indeed, fratricidal combat took place in which both Allied and Axis "Dewos" battled each other in response to the Allied landings in North Africa.
The little Dewo is a potent fighter and provides a challenge in fights against the Bf 109E, its main adversary. Highly maneuverable and possessing very good zoom climb ability after a dive, the D.520 can be fought with effectively throughout a campaign.
It has poor acceleration and getting slow can exacerbate a disadvantage against an enemy with better power loading like the Bf 109F or Fw 190. The gun package is very effective. Although the 20mm cannon has limited ammunition at only 60 rounds, when you use the cannon as the finishing touch on a gun solution where the machine guns are hitting, the results can be devastating.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor MAX. SPEED: 540 km/h WEIGHT: 2,800 kg CREW: 1 ARMAMENT: 20 mm Hispano Cannon (1) 7.5 mm MAC LMGs (4)
